region: Romulus · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Buttonwood Grove sits on the west shore of Cayuga Lake in Romulus, about ninety minutes from Syracuse. Founded in 2004 by Ken and Diane Riemer, it was bought in 2014 by Dave and Melissa Pittard, who both grew up in Skaneateles. Dave learned farming and his first winemaking, with apples, at his family’s Beak & Skiff orchard in Lafayette before studying at Cornell’s College of Agriculture. Since taking over, the Pittards have built a new winemaking facility, roughly tripled the vineyard and renovated the tasting room; their 2016 Riesling won the 2017 Governor’s Cup as New York’s best wine.

The estate’s established vineyards grow Riesling, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, and its newer plantings include Gewürztraminer, an aromatic grape that does well in the cool, lake-moderated climate of the Finger Lakes. The 2022 shows the grape’s signature perfume: floral and zesty, with lychee, honeycomb and a note of white pepper, and a bright, crisp finish.
